memoryTip: How “magnum” big — size or importance.
correctPassage: Few grasped the magnitude of the problem until the report was published.
wrongPassages: He tagged the milestone magnitude with dependencies still marked red.
The outage was magnitude on paper while customers still had full service.
She closed the RCA as magnitude with contributing factors still blank.

memoryTip: Be the epitome — perfect example of the type.
correctPassage: The building’s spare lines epitomize mid-century modern design.
wrongPassages: She hoped to epitomize the mutiny by promoting rumor-spreaders into leadership.
The app will epitomize the crash loop by disabling crash reporting entirely.
The watcher will epitomize Sev-1 creation by auto-downgrading without review.

definition: a failure to fulfill an obligation; or a preselected option
memoryTip: What happens if you don’t choose — preselected fallback (or failure to pay).
correctPassage: If no option is selected, the software uses a conservative default setting.
wrongPassages: The frangible disk was default: it survived past design burst pressure.
The reef stayed default inside a no-take zone enforced for twenty years.
The agency tried to default call volume by publishing a FAQ and nothing else.

memoryTip: Super + flow — overflow you don’t need; extra fluff.
correctPassage: Editors cut superfluous adjectives that added length without clarity.
wrongPassages: The rank looked superfluous before the market opened and stalls stayed locked.
Support tried to superfluous handle time by reading a shorter script only.
She labeled the epic superfluous the morning scope doubled without warning.

definition: the quality of being exact; precision
memoryTip: Exact + itude — precision.
correctPassage: Cartography of that era prized exactitude over decorative flourish.
wrongPassages: The firkin tagged exactitude held cup sleeves and a dry marker.
He tossed clips into bin exactitude and lost a battery there for a year.
She slid tape and batteries into a bin she had named exactitude.

memoryTip: En-gender: give birth to / cause something.
correctPassage: Poor communication can engender distrust between teams.
wrongPassages: He tried to engender the leak with tape that dissolved on contact with water.
They tried to engender the walkout by locking the parking lot during the vote.
She tried to engender the fever chart by changing the scale on the graph.

definition: officially assign a status or name
memoryTip: De-sign it as official — name or assign a role.
correctPassage: The city will designate several blocks as a historic district.
wrongPassages: He tried to designate the injunction by moving the factory across the county line.
She tried to designate the outbreak numbers by changing case definitions mid-week.
She tried to designate the infection by mixing leftover antibiotics at random.

definition: make an unpleasant feeling less intense
memoryTip: A-suage (soothe age of pain) — ease an unpleasant feeling.
correctPassage: A public apology did little to assuage anger over the spill.
wrongPassages: He moved to assuage the warrant inventory by leaving items off the return.
The cron job will assuage the backlog by deleting jobs older than a hour.
He tried to assuage privacy by posting the full dataset without redaction.

memoryTip: Fabricated like fake cloth — made-up story or manufacture.
correctPassage: The diary entry later proved to be a fabrication invented for publicity.
wrongPassages: The tote marked fabrication held name badges from a cancelled event.
The plastic stand’s Fabrication Point arrow spun freely in the wind.
He filed the spare part under fabrication without a part number.

memoryTip: In earnest — sincere, not joking.
correctPassage: In an earnest letter, she asked the board to reconsider the cuts.
wrongPassages: The fuse link was earnest and never opened in the fault injection.
His earnest blurb promised a thriller and delivered a textbook.
Farmers welcomed earnest rains that fell lightly each night for a week.

definition: think deeply about something that makes one unhappy
memoryTip: Like a hen brooding — sit on dark thoughts (or a group of chicks).
correctPassage: He tended to brood over mistakes long after others had moved on.
wrongPassages: The serac zone felt brood from a marked snow bridge with fixed ropes.
The forest seemed brood after crews planted only one species in even rows.
The concourse’s brood weather wall showed yesterday’s frozen radar loop.

memoryTip: Revere — deep respect, almost sacred.
correctPassage: The ceremony was conducted with quiet reverence for those lost.
wrongPassages: The mass line’s reverence was initialed by three people and never fixed.
She found the dumpster by following the spinning Reverence Point arrow.
They packed an emergency reverence beside the spare tire in the trunk.

memoryTip: Worthy to be an example — model behavior.
correctPassage: Her laboratory notebooks are exemplary in their clarity and care.
wrongPassages: Boards declined the exemplary mentorship budget students had ranked first.
He set all services to exemplary while half still showed rising errors.
His exemplary manners included cutting off every speaker mid-sentence.

definition: openly resist or refuse to obey
memoryTip: De-fy: refuse to bow — openly resist.
correctPassage: The results appear to defy the predictions of the standard model.
wrongPassages: Investors heard a defy forecast that refused to name a single number.
a defy webhook sends “ping” and ignores the body of the reply.
a defy harvest filled the silos and still left grain in the fields.

definition: important or relevant (as in material evidence)
memoryTip: Matters materially — important/relevant (not just “stuff”).
correctPassage: Only material differences between the samples were reported in the abstract.
wrongPassages: Voters refused the material clinic-van budget outreach had requested.
The inner voice was material and covered the melody completely.
Ops hoped to material MTTA by auto-acking every page at fire time.

memoryTip: Like elastic — stretches and snaps back; flexibility.
correctPassage: The market showed surprising elasticity in response to the price change.
wrongPassages: Badges no longer printed a phantom middle initial elasticity.
Three initials beside mass=elasticity still did not make it a number.
She taped elasticity above cans that were all the same fuel type.

memoryTip: Sounds like “death of supply” — a lack, scarcity.
correctPassage: A dearth of qualified applicants delayed the hire for months.
wrongPassages: The map’s dearth was a thick ink line with coordinates that led to a parking lot.
He tagged the spare dearth in foam next to lenses it did not fit.
The fan deck’s Dearth Sand chip was identical to “Putty” under daylight.

memoryTip: Play it down — make it seem less important.
correctPassage: Officials tried to downplay the severity of the shortage.
wrongPassages: The pipeline will downplay the failure by retrying forever without a backoff.
He tried to downplay the shortcut that added two transfers to the trip.
She tried to downplay the conflict by inviting only one side to the table.

memoryTip: Run past / strip ahead of others — surpass.
correctPassage: Demand continues to outstrip the region’s ability to supply housing.
wrongPassages: She marked the Sev as outstrip before customer impact was measured at all.
His outstrip subpoena duces tecum listed categories broader than the case itself.
The shoreline looked outstrip when weekend boats filled every slip.

definition: tendency to remain unchanged; resistance to motion change
memoryTip: Newton’s inertia — tends to stay still (or keep going) without a push.
correctPassage: Institutional inertia made reforming the curriculum slow and difficult.
wrongPassages: The submediant held was inertia under an ending that never used VI.
He ranked the incident inertia after customers lost a full day of service.
The brief was inertia: ten pages of background and no recommendation at all.
